cells.tense: The deciding is here and running, and the weight it bears is held on purpose.
cells.ask: Offer one more piece of input than is comfortable, and see whether the answer comes back useful.
cells.core:
You can hold a line and move the room at the same time. When this is steady, the call lands and what rests on you keeps its footing after — no one left guessing, nothing dropped while you decide, and people around you can feel that both are happening at once. Even here there's a weight in it: some of what rests on you, nobody asked you to lift.

What's open now is more input. Ask the question you half-know the answer to, say the part you'd normally keep private, and let the response land before deciding what it's for. One more voice reaching the next move doesn't loosen the line — it sharpens where the line goes.
cells.sheetLine: You hold the line and move it at the same time.
cells.verb: Deciding and moving first, before anyone else has to.
cells.place: The part of a life that holds weight without breaking.

cells.tense: The deciding is still going, but it's running somewhere ahead of now, steeling against a day that hasn't arrived.
cells.ask: Plan only the opening of one real conversation and leave the other person's answer unwritten.
cells.core:
You run next week's arguments before the week gets here. Each talk gets rehearsed against an objection nobody's raised, every move checked twice, and the bracing uses up what you'd need to stand behind the decision once it's actually made. The pushing has gotten ahead of what's in front of you.

When it's landing well, this is real strength saved for real pressure — a line held when it matters. Point it at the decision that's already here. Pick the conversation that's next, write your first sentence, and stop there. Their side stays blank on purpose; the rehearsal is what's costing you, not the bearing.

cells.tense: The deciding went quiet a while back, and the body is still standing at the door it left through.
cells.ask: Name one change that would make a single part of your week easier, and put it in one sentence to the person it touches.
cells.core:
There's weight here still being carried and no push behind it. Decisions arrive already made by someone else, the line doesn't get drawn, and what holds everything up has stopped being aimed anywhere. What's missing isn't nerve in the moment — it's motion, the thing that keeps the deciding from going dormant.

When it's landing well, this is quiet power in a body: bearing what has to be borne without going hard. Start with the smallest change that would lighten one part of your day. Not the whole reorganising — a single sentence today, naming what moves. The deciding starts again in the saying, and less sits alone on you once the line is on the table.

cells.tense: The deciding is running the room, and the hand that's doing it wouldn't say it's a hand.
cells.ask: Name one thing you set up that people still follow, and say who decided it.
cells.core:
You've already set the terms of what moves here — how work gets picked up, how a room is run, what gets started and what gets left. From outside, it looks like the situation deciding itself: the demands, the deadlines, the way things have to go. Something decided, and it isn't being claimed.

When it's landing well, this is structure that serves what it holds: clear, steady, and people can find their footing in it. Pick one thing that's clearly you — a rule people follow, a direction that's carrying — and say who put it there. Not a brag, just the name on it. Claimed, it can also be changed, released or handed off; nothing steering invisibly can be steered.
cells.sheetLine: You already built the conditions. You just haven't signed them.
